title: Fix and finish your AI-built app
metaTitle: Fix Your Lovable, Bolt or Cursor App | Shair Ali
description: Stuck with an app built in Lovable, Bolt, Cursor or Claude Code? Shair Ali fixes the bugs, secures it and ships it to production on your own server.
intro: AI builders get you a working demo fast. Getting from that demo to something paying users can trust is a different job: real authentication, payments that don't double-charge, data that's protected, and a deployment you control. That's the part I do.
problems: The app works in the preview but breaks once real users sign up
Login, roles or database rules are leaking data or locking people out
Stripe payments or webhooks fire twice, or not at all
Every new prompt fixes one thing and breaks two others
You want to move off the builder's hosting onto your own server or AWS
deliverables: A written audit of the codebase: what's broken, what's risky, what to keep
Fixes for authentication, access control and data validation
Payments and webhooks made reliable (verified, idempotent, logged)
Clean-up of duplicated, AI-generated code so it can be maintained
Deployment to your own server or cloud with SSL, monitoring and CI/CD
A handover: how it works, how to deploy, what to build next

proof.text: Took over a live 2021 codebase I didn't write and modernized it while it stayed online: hardened security, rebuilt payments with verified Stripe webhooks, and added one-push deploys.
Built billing that can't drift: the server is the source of truth, and payments are protected against duplicates at the database level.

faq.q: Which AI tools do you work with?
faq.a: Apps started in Lovable, Bolt, v0, Cursor, Replit or Claude Code. Underneath they're usually React or Next.js with Supabase, Firebase or a Node API, which is my everyday stack.

faq.q: Do I have to start over?
faq.a: Rarely. I start with an audit, keep what's solid and fix or replace the parts that put your users or data at risk. You get a clear list before any big change.

faq.q: Can you move my app off Lovable or Bolt hosting?
faq.a: Yes. I can deploy it to your own VPS, DigitalOcean or AWS with a domain, SSL and automatic deploys from GitHub, so you own the whole setup.
Send me the repo or a link to the app and a short list of what's broken. I'll reply with what it needs and a fixed quote.

title: Deploy your Next.js or Node.js app to production
metaTitle: Deploy Next.js & Node.js Apps to AWS or a VPS | Shair Ali
description: Shair Ali deploys Next.js and Node.js apps to AWS, DigitalOcean or any VPS with Nginx, PM2, SSL and one-push CI/CD from GitHub, then keeps them running.
intro: Your app runs on your laptop. I get it running on a real server: a domain, HTTPS, a process manager that restarts it when it crashes, and deploys that happen with a git push instead of a nervous SSH session.
problems: The app works locally but you don't know how to put it online
Deploys are manual and something breaks every time
SSL, DNS or the Nginx config is wrong and the site is down
Hosting bills on serverless platforms are climbing
Nobody is watching the server once it's live
deliverables: Server setup on AWS EC2, DigitalOcean, Hetzner or any Ubuntu VPS
Nginx reverse proxy, HTTPS certificates and DNS
PM2 process management with automatic restarts
CI/CD with GitHub Actions: build, migrate and restart on every push
Environment and secrets set up properly, with no keys in the repo
Health checks and a short runbook so you know what to do if something fails

proof.text: Push-to-deploy CI/CD on AWS EC2 with Nginx and PM2: GitHub Actions connects over SSH, installs, builds and restarts with no downtime.
One-push deploys for two apps on an Ubuntu VPS: GitHub Actions builds both, runs migrations, restarts PM2 and reloads Nginx.

faq.a: For most small products a single VPS (DigitalOcean, Hetzner or AWS EC2) with Nginx and PM2 is cheaper and simpler than serverless. I'll recommend based on your traffic and budget.

faq.q: Will my site go down during the move?
faq.a: No. I set up and test the new server first, then switch DNS once everything works.
Yes. I can keep watching updates, certificates, backups and uptime after launch, which is how most of my clients work with me.

title: AI chatbots and WhatsApp assistants for your business
metaTitle: AI Chatbot & WhatsApp Assistant Developer | Shair Ali
description: Shair Ali builds AI assistants trained on your business that answer customers 24/7 on your website and WhatsApp, and hand over to a person when needed.
intro: Your customers ask the same questions every day, often outside office hours. I build AI assistants that answer them from your own information, on your website and on WhatsApp, and pass the conversation to your team when a person is needed.
problems: Your team answers the same questions about prices, availability and policies
Messages arrive at night and in other languages
Generic chatbots give wrong answers about your business
You want customers on WhatsApp without someone watching the phone
deliverables: An assistant grounded in your own content: FAQs, prices, policies, documents
Website chat widget and WhatsApp integration
Hand-over to a human, plus conversation logs you can review
Multilingual replies for international customers
Hosting on your own server with your own API keys

proof.text: An AI assistant tuned to a Sicilian hotel's own information, answering guests 24/7 on the website and on WhatsApp.
A built-in AI support assistant running on Groq's Llama 3.1, with Gemini as a fallback.

faq.q: Which AI models do you use?
faq.a: OpenAI, Groq (Llama), Gemini or Claude, depending on cost, speed and language. I usually set up a fallback model so the assistant stays available.

faq.q: Will it make things up about my business?
faq.a: It answers from the information you provide and is told to hand over to a person when it isn't sure. I test it on your real questions before launch.

faq.q: Can it book or take orders?
faq.a: Yes, it can connect to your booking system, CRM or a simple form through an API or an automation tool such as n8n.

title: AI automation and agents for repetitive work
metaTitle: AI Automation & n8n Workflow Developer | Shair Ali
description: Shair Ali automates repetitive work with AI agents, n8n workflows and custom integrations: quotes, emails, documents, CRM updates and alerts.
intro: If someone on your team copies data between tools, writes the same emails or builds the same documents every week, that work can usually be automated. I connect your tools with n8n or custom code and add AI where it saves real time.
problems: Staff copy data between forms, spreadsheets, email and your CRM
Quotes, receipts or reports are built by hand
Leads wait hours for a reply
You've tried no-code tools but the workflows keep breaking
deliverables: A map of the manual steps worth automating, with time saved for each
n8n workflows or custom Node.js services, self-hosted if you prefer
AI steps for classifying, summarising, drafting and extracting data
Integrations with Stripe, email, CRMs, spreadsheets and WhatsApp
Error alerts and logs so failures don't go unnoticed

proof.text: In-house tools that automate the hotel's quotes and receipts, alongside its AI guest assistant.
Thirteen automated email flows that move each lien request from intake and payment through to delivery.

faq.a: n8n when you want flexibility and self-hosting, Zapier or Make for simple flows, and custom code when the logic is complex or needs to be very reliable. I'll suggest the cheapest option that works.
Every workflow I build has error handling and sends an alert, so a failure is noticed and fixed instead of silently losing data.

faq.q: Can you host it for me?
faq.a: Yes, on your own server or a small VPS, so you're not paying per task.

title: Real-time chat, voice and video apps
metaTitle: WebRTC Developer for Chat, Voice & Video Apps | Shair Ali
description: Shair Ali builds real-time chat, voice and video apps with WebRTC, LiveKit and Socket.IO, including consultation marketplaces with per-minute billing.
intro: Live features are where many apps fall apart: dropped calls, timers that drift, billing that doesn't match the session. I build real-time products where the server keeps the truth, so calls, chat and payments stay in sync.
problems: You need video or voice calls inside your app, not a Zoom link
Sessions must be billed by the minute, accurately
Chat, notifications and presence need to update instantly
Your current real-time feature is unreliable under load
deliverables: Video and voice calls with WebRTC (LiveKit) and real-time chat with Socket.IO
Presence, typing indicators, notifications and live dashboards
Wallets, per-minute metering and Stripe top-ups
Scheduling with automatic session start and end
Admin and provider consoles for running the marketplace

proof.text: A pay-per-minute expert marketplace in Italy with chat, voice and video in one place: 1,250+ commits, 180+ API endpoints, and billing that can't drift.

keywords: pay per minute video consultation app

faq.q: Do you use LiveKit, Twilio or plain WebRTC?
faq.a: Usually LiveKit for video and voice because it scales and handles bad networks well, Twilio for phone and SMS, and Socket.IO for chat and live updates.

faq.q: How is per-minute billing kept accurate?
faq.a: The server meters every session and is the source of truth; the browser only displays the timer. Payments are deduplicated so nobody is charged twice.

faq.q: Can you add video to my existing app?
faq.a: Yes. I can add calls, chat or live updates to an existing React or Node.js product without rebuilding it.
